title: Jamshedpur Auto & Auto Components: a note to the credit manager
narrative: Cash sits in receivables and inventory, not in the plant. The plant is presses, CNCs and dies — capex is lumpy and die-specific, so a supplier's asset is only worth what the next order book says.

## What has changed now
**National auto-component output is running hot: IIP NIC 29 output +25.2% YoY and +19.2% Apr-to-date [D].** Peer results confirm demand — Motherson Sumi Wiring net profit up 35% to Rs 223 crore with revenue up 46.7% to Rs 4,054 crore [4], and Lumax lifted its growth guidance after a strong first half [7]. But margins are the weak spot: ASK Automotive posted record revenue while aluminium squeezed margins [5], and Elara expects Q4FY26 auto EBITDA growth of about 21% with commodity risks rising [6]. Locally, the signal is consumption-led — a Land Cruiser worth Rs 2.5 crore sold in Jamshedpur on Dhanteras, with EV and hybrid demand rising [1] — and Tata Motors' Jamshedpur plant agreed a 14% bonus with 151 new FTAs hired [2]. **So when a proposal lands, check the customer's commodity pass-through clause; if aluminium or steel is unhedged and unbilled, ask for the last three months' price-variation invoices.**

## Where the growth is
**Bank credit is growing +27.0% YoY against output +19.2%, a 7.8 pp gap [D] — money is chasing this sector faster than it is producing.** Jharkhand's electricity demand is up 15.2% Apr-to-date versus India's 9.5% [D], a real local tailwind. Pursue Tier-2/Tier-3 units with EV-agnostic products — braking, lightweighting, aluminium — where ASK reports substantial EV order wins [5]. Avoid units concentrated on engine and related parts; rating commentary flags higher obsolescence risk as EVs spread [11]. **If a borrower's order book is one OEM and one part family, ask for the customer-wise sales split before you sanction.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the working-capital cycle, not the P&L.** Rating commentary notes gross current assets averaging 160-170 days [10], so size the drawing power on that reality. Take monthly stock-and-debtor statements, quarterly GST returns, and a die/order-book confirmation from the OEM. **If Debt/EBITDA crosses 2.5-2.75 times on debt-funded capex, ask for the capex phasing and OEM letter of intent before enhancing limits [10].** Cap single-OEM exposure and take a second charge on dies where possible.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch receivable days against the OEM's payment cycle and inventory build against order releases.** A supplier whose billing slows while its OEM parent is hiring [2] is a supplier losing share, not a supplier waiting for demand. Watch commodity-led gross margin compression [5][6] and any shift in the borrower's part mix toward engine components [11]. Local coverage of this cluster is thin — the Adityapur detail comes from a single LinkedIn post [3], so lean on first principles and peer results for the rest.
